body.text: Why is Selçuk a smarter base for Ephesus than Kuşadası?

Selçuk puts you five minutes by taxi or dolmuş from the Lower Gate of [UNESCO-listed Ephesus](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1018/), letting you enter at opening time before cruise-ship coaches arrive from Kuşadası (20 kilometers away). You also trade multi-story resort blocks and souvenir-touting port streets for a quiet market town with direct rail links to İzmir.

Staying overnight in Selçuk means you can tour Ephesus early in cool morning light, return to town for lunch and a midday rest, and spend the late afternoon walking to Ayasuluk Hill without booking a single private transfer. Unlike Kuşadası, whose waterfront rhythm peaks around cruise disembarkation schedules, Selçuk operates as a working agricultural town surrounded by peach orchards and olive groves. Travelers moving down from northern Ottoman cities like [Bursa](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/destinations/bursa) appreciate Selçuk's calm evening pace.
What major sights sit within walking distance in Selçuk?

Five major historical sites cluster within a 15-minute walk of Selçuk's train station: the [Basilica of St. John and Ayasuluk Castle](https://muze.gov.tr/muze-detay?SectionId=STJ01&DistId=STJ), the 14th-century İsa Bey Mosque, the Ephesus Archaeological Museum, the Temple of Artemis foundations, and the Roman aqueduct pillars where white storks nest each spring.

Built by Byzantine Emperor Justinian in the 6th century over the traditional tomb of the Apostle John, the Basilica of St. John crowns Ayasuluk Hill with commanding views across the Küçük Menderes plain. Immediately below its western slope stands İsa Bey Mosque (1375), a serene Anatolian Beylik masterpiece constructed partly from reused Ephesus marble. A five-minute stroll south brings you to the [Ephesus Archaeological Museum](https://www.turkishmuseums.com/blog/detail/5-must-see-places-in-ephesus/10057/4), home to the monumental Artemis statues and Terrace House frescoes, followed by the solitary standing column of the Temple of Artemis.

body.text: How does the direct train from İzmir Airport (ADB) work?

Turkish State Railways (TCDD) operates [direct regional trains from İzmir Adnan Menderes Airport (ADB) station to Selçuk Station](https://www.rome2rio.com/Train/Izmir-Airport-ADB/Sel%C3%A7uk-Station) several times daily, covering the route in roughly 58 to 65 minutes with no transfers. If your flight lands between TCDD departures, the suburban İZBAN commuter line runs south from the same airport platform with one straightforward cross-platform transfer at Tepeköy.

Follow the covered pedestrian bridge directly out of ADB's domestic terminal to the elevated railway platform. TCDD regional tickets are inexpensive and sold at the platform booth or via the TCDD e-Bilet app, while İZBAN uses an İzmirim Kart purchased at station kiosks. Selçuk's historic station drops you right in the center of town—five minutes on foot from most boutique guesthouses.

items: Enter Ephesus at 08:00 (or late afternoon after 15:30) to avoid peak cruise-bus crowds on Curetes Street.
Buy the combined ticket that includes Ephesus Terrace Houses; their Roman mosaics and wall paintings are the site's highlight.
Wear modest attire (shoulders and knees covered) when stepping into İsa Bey Mosque outside prayer times.
Check TCDD departure times before boarding your flight to İzmir so you know whether to catch a direct train or İZBAN.
Consider a 15-minute dolmuş ride up to Şirince village in the late afternoon for hillside views and coffee.

body.text: Where do locals eat çöp şiş and Aegean dishes?

Selçuk is famous across İzmir province for çöp şiş—small cubes of marinated lamb threaded onto thin wooden skewers, grilled over oak charcoal, and served on flatbread with roasted peppers, tomatoes, and sumac onions. Local favorites cluster along Atatürk Caddesi and the side streets behind the aqueduct, alongside simple lokanta kitchens serving olive-oil seasonal greens.

Well-known town fixtures such as Ejder Restaurant and Eski İstasyon draw local families for charcoal-grilled çöp şiş and ayran without resort markups. For lunch, step into a neighborhood esnaf lokantası (tradesman's diner) near the bus station to pick from daily pots of stuffed zucchini blossoms, braised okra, artichoke hearts, and lentil soup at straightforward local prices.

faq.q: How many nights should you stay in Selçuk?
faq.a: Two nights (one full day plus an arrival afternoon) give you enough time to tour Ephesus and the Terrace Houses without rushing, visit St. John Basilica, İsa Bey Mosque, and the Ephesus Museum, and make a short trip to Şirince.

faq.q: Can you walk from Selçuk to Ephesus?
faq.a: Yes. A tree-lined pedestrian path runs roughly 3 kilometers from Selçuk town center past the Temple of Artemis to the Lower Gate of Ephesus (about 35 to 40 minutes on foot), though frequent dolmuş minibuses make the trip in five minutes.

faq.q: Is the House of the Virgin Mary walkable from Selçuk?
faq.a: No. It sits about 9 kilometers uphill on Mount Koressos (Bülbül Dağı), requiring a 15-minute taxi ride or private car from Selçuk.

faq.q: Does İsa Bey Mosque charge an entrance fee?
faq.a: No. İsa Bey Mosque is an active place of worship with free entry outside daily prayer times; small voluntary donations help support upkeep.

faq.q: Are there direct trains from Selçuk to Denizli for Pamukkale?
faq.a: Yes. Direct TCDD regional trains run several times a day from Selçuk Station east through the Büyük Menderes valley to Denizli in roughly 3 hours 15 minutes, making an easy car-free link to Pamukkale.

faq.q: Is Selçuk's Saturday market worth visiting?
faq.a: Yes. Every Saturday morning, farmers from surrounding villages set up produce, fig, olive, and spice stalls across central Selçuk—ideal for sampling dried Aegean figs and local cheeses.
